name: Dakota Hope
event: UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs. Nolan
summary: Aggressive, powerful regional finisher (11-2; former Peak Fighting featherweight champion) whose UFC debut was a short-notice split-decision loss to Kai Kamaka III at lightweight in April. Back down to featherweight and again on short notice, replacing Gaston Bolanos against Francis Marshall. Never been stopped.

how_they_fight.Striking: Front-foot pressure: backs opponents to the cage with short punches, body knees and clinch elbows (Cageside Press). Dropped Kamaka with a right hand in R1 and stunned him with a right hook in R2. Busy (106 of 258 significant strikes against Kamaka) but loose: Kamaka landed 105 of 159, so he gets hit a lot for the volume he throws. Five R1 knockouts on the regionals; Heavy calls it "vicious power".
how_they_fight.Grappling: Mostly a striker who clinches. Has a fifth-round submission (Patrick Connors, Peak Fighting title fight) and landed a late takedown on Kamaka, but takedowns are not his main route.
how_they_fight.Defense: Durability is good: 13 pro fights and never stopped (both losses are decisions). Defense is the issue: he walks through return fire, and Kamaka out-worked him on the body and with counters late.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Fast starter. All five KO wins came in R1 (0:15 to 1:59); his only submission came in R5. The other five wins and both losses went the distance. He has gone 25 minutes three times on the regionals, yet against Kamaka his pace dipped in R2 and he was visibly tired in R3, leaning on the clinch and overreaching (Cageside Press) - he won R1 and lost the fight over R2-R3. Short notice twice in a row is worth keeping in mind for R3.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Commits to pressure and finishing; when the early storm doesn't land, he hasn't shown a plan B beyond more of the same. Took both UFC fights on short notice.

patterns: Early pressure and power: wins R1, five R1 KO wins
If it goes long he tends to fade; decision record 5-2
Never finished: both losses are decisions (Bosnick, Kamaka split)
Clinch work against the fence: knees to the body, elbows
concerns: R2-R3 cardio at UFC pace (faded vs Kamaka)
Absorbs a lot of strikes: 4.95 absorbed a minute
Second short-notice booking, and a cut back down to featherweight after debuting at lightweight
keys_to_beat: Survive the first five minutes; make him work at range
Body work and counters as he comes forward - Kamaka's recipe
Bank R2 and R3 once his pace drops

news.text: Steps in for Gaston Bolanos (eyebrow cut in training) against Francis Marshall at featherweight; the official UFC page still listed Bolanos on Oct 20. Sources disagree on weight class (featherweight per Heavy, bantamweight in some listings).
Lost UFC debut to Kai Kamaka III by split decision (29-28, 28-29, 29-28) at lightweight after dropping him in R1.
